matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old `GET /pulls/:id` endpoint fetched the latest files, commits, and body from GitHub on every request (falling back to persisted data on error). The new version serves only what is already stored in the database, never making a network call. Any external caller that relied on the GET to implicitly refresh PR data will now receive stale data until they explicitly call `POST /pulls/:id/refresh`. While the response schema is identical, the side-effect contract has changed. The client in this PR is updated to use the new refresh endpoint, but other consumers (e.g., CI runners, integrations) are not.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub
findings.rationale: The old GET endpoint attempted to fetch the latest files, commits, and body from GitHub on every request, falling back to persisted data only on error. The new GET endpoint always serves persisted data without any GitHub call. Any caller that relied on the GET returning fresh data (e.g., an e2e test that expects the latest PR state after a GitHub push) will now receive stale data until it explicitly calls POST /pulls/:id/refresh. The client in this PR is updated to use the new refresh button, but other callers (CI runner, external integrations) are not shown and may break silently. The compatible alternative is to keep the old GET behavior but add a query parameter (e.g., `?refresh=true`) to trigger a GitHub fetch, or to leave GET unchanged and only add the new POST endpoint for explicit refresh.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub; response is always stale and may lack fields

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer fetches fresh data from GitHub; response is always stale and may lack fields
findings.rationale: The old GET always attempted a live GitHub fetch and, on success, returned the full GitHub API response (including fields like `labels`, `milestone`, `draft`, etc.) after persisting it. On failure it fell back to the database subset. The new GET always returns only the database subset and never contacts GitHub. A deployed caller that polls GET to get fresh PR data (e.g., after a merge) will now silently receive stale data. A caller that reads extra fields like `labels` from the response will now get `undefined`. Both are silent behavior changes that break callers without any code change on their side.
